name: Andy Burnham
role: Labour MP for Leigh (2001–2017), Mayor of Greater Manchester (2017–2026), Prime Minister and Labour leader (from July 2026)
summary: A Labour soft-left politician who calls himself a socialist and a Co-operative Party member. He favours devolution, public control of utilities and transport, proportional representation and an elected second chamber, and supports eventually rejoining the EU, while taking a more cautious line on immigration, welfare reform, fiscal rules and single-sex spaces in recent years.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Served as Health Secretary and proposed a publicly funded National Care Service; voted against GPs buying services and for limits on private patient work in the NHS.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: His 2015 leadership platform extended the higher minimum wage to under-25s ('true living wage for all ages').

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Favours stronger public control of energy, water, housing and transport and state intervention in northern industry rather than leaving allocation to markets.

public-ownership.rationale: Pledged progressive railway renationalisation (2015), backs public ownership of Thames Water, and in 2026 wants stronger public control of energy, housing, water and transport, which he describes as short of full nationalisation.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Proposed restoring the 50p top rate in 2015 and voted for a higher rate on income over £150,000; in 2026 he pledged not to raise income tax, VAT or employee NICs while backing land value and council tax reform.

unions-good.rationale: Voted consistently against tighter regulation of trade unions.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Proposed banning water-company bill rises by cancelling dividends and backs banning bonuses across water company leadership teams, citing excessive profiteering.

cut-welfare.rationale: Voted almost always against reducing welfare spending and for raising benefits with prices; in 2026 he wants to reduce the welfare bill through council-run support into work rather than cuts.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Voted consistently for Labour anti-terror laws, ID cards, retention of communications data and mostly for mass communications surveillance.

state-harmful.rationale: Record in government and as mayor is of active state provision and public control; no sign of a view that the state is unnecessary or harmful.

empower-police-military.rationale: Says defence spending must rise to meet NATO obligations; no statement on police authority.

decide-locally.rationale: Strong advocate of devolution and voted mostly for more powers for councils; wants fiscal devolution such as local tourist taxes.

traditional-family.rationale: In a 2007 interview said children are better off in a home with married parents and the tax system may recognise marriage; he also supports same-sex marriage.

abortion-legal.rationale: Voted almost always for easing restrictions on abortion access.

reduce-immigration.rationale: In 2026 said net migration needs to fall further and backed the thrust of indefinite leave to remain reforms, having earlier opposed caps.

nation-first.rationale: Says he will always put Britain's interest first, but also says control comes through collaboration with partners.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Mixed: voted for the 2003 Iraq war, defending it in 2010, later said he regrets it; in 2015 would not rule out intervention in Syria; criticised the 2026 Iran war.

open-borders.rationale: Supports reducing net migration and backed Home Secretary efforts to limit immigration.

limit-growth.rationale: Frames net zero as compatible with and a route to growth; his programme is 'good growth in every postcode'.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Voted mostly for measures to prevent climate change.

land-value-tax.rationale: Proposed a land value tax at the heart of tax reform to replace stamp duty (2010) and a land value tax on commercial property (2015), not most other taxes.

tax-inheritance.rationale: His 2010 platform would have replaced inheritance tax with a land value tax and in 2026 he floated a care levy to replace it, though he would revisit the farm inheritance tax change selectively. Ambiguous on heavy taxation of large estates.

state-directs-investment.rationale: In 2016 argued for leaving the single market partly to allow more state intervention in northern industry.

direct-votes.rationale: Says referendums divide households and communities and must be approached with great care; told devolved leaders he is focused on practical measures, not further referendums.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Long-standing Labour Friends of Israel supporter who backs a two-state solution; does not directly address this statement.

school-vouchers.rationale: Opposed free schools as shadow education secretary and voted mostly against greater school autonomy and academies; vouchers themselves are not addressed.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Says he will not take risks with public finances, backs sound public finances and the fiscal rules, while arguing preventative spending pays back.

national-self-determination.rationale: Called for recognition of a Palestinian state and backs a two-state solution; opposed 'ugly' nationalism in the UK context.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: In 2015 said freedom to work should not mean freedom to claim and proposed restrictions on newcomers' access to benefits and housing; in 2026 stood back from scrapping no recourse to public funds.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Wants some support to be conditional on taking up opportunities offered, while insisting people receive the right support first.

class-collaboration.rationale: Describes the Greater Manchester way as partnership across public, private, community, faith and trade unions pulling in the same direction.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Says the UK will have to use oil and gas for some time and the North Sea should bridge to clean energy; reported plans for new drilling, while committing to net zero.

proportional-representation.rationale: Favours proportional representation for Westminster, though in 2026 said it should be put to voters in a manifesto first.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Says Westminster politics is out of touch and 'makes a fraud out of good people', while praising MPs as good people.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Championed the Hillsborough Independent Panel and the Hillsborough Law on public authority accountability.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Advocates a preventative state with public ownership of essentials, a national care service, council homes and an NHS.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Voted for same-sex marriage and almost always for measures expanding LGBT+ rights.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Argues the loss of council homes since the 1980s and Right to Buy's effects on the rental sector drive housing costs; plans the biggest council-house building programme since the war.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Voted consistently against tighter regulation of trade unions; secret-ballot rules specifically not addressed.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Wants to loosen the whip system and criticised suspensions of MPs.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Said in 2025 he hopes to see the UK rejoin the EU in his lifetime and in 2026 supports rejoining in the long term, but not reopening Brexit now; mostly voted for greater EU integration.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Said in 2015 he would resign from the shadow cabinet if Labour backed leaving NATO.

death-penalty.rationale: Called public executions abhorrent and said he would never support them; no general statement on capital punishment.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: As PM, funded part of the £2 bus fare cap by turning international climate-related donations into loans.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Backs a two-state solution and opposes West Bank settlements.

collective-defense.rationale: Said in 2015 he would resign from the shadow cabinet if Labour backed leaving NATO.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Condemned Russia's 2014 annexation of Crimea and says Russia must not prevail in Ukraine; calls West Bank settlements illegal.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Voted mostly for removing hereditary peers from the Lords and always for a wholly elected Lords; monarchy not addressed.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: In 2009 he moved health policy toward a preference for the public NHS, but he also works through voluntary-sector and private partners in Greater Manchester.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Earlier supported trans people using facilities matching their gender; in May 2026 backed single-sex facility rules following For Women Scotland and the EHRC guidance. Position on legal recognition itself is not stated.

assisted-dying.rationale: Abstained in 2015; said in 2024 he would back the principle; as PM in July 2026 declined to give a stance, saying palliative and social care funding must be fixed first.

social-market-economy.rationale: Describes 'business-friendly socialism': sound finances and stability for business alongside public intervention and social protection.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Supports higher defence spending and NATO commitments; says defence must be a bigger part of public spending.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Supports NATO membership (2015 resignation pledge) and consistent support for Ukraine.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: In 2015 urged Pope Francis to bring the Church into the 21st century on gay rights.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Voted consistently for replacing Trident, which is based in the UK.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Brought buses under public franchise control (Bee Network), backs public ownership of Thames Water, and voted against marketising NHS purchasing.

second-chamber.rationale: Wants the Lords replaced with a Senate of Regions and Nations including metro mayors; voted always for a wholly elected Lords.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Voted for the 2003 Iraq war (later said he would not vote for it again) and mostly for UK combat operations overseas.

free-public-college.rationale: Pledged in 2015 to scrap tuition fees; earlier backed a graduate tax replacing fees, and voted against raising the fee cap to £9,000.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Pledges to stick to the government's fiscal rules and cites their discipline, though not specifically as legally binding limits.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: On Gaza said evidence suggests war crimes may have been committed and accountability is a matter for the international courts.

close-ties-china.rationale: Says Britain should keep dialogue open with China and backed Starmer's state visit; as mayor supported cooperation on green technology.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: As PM scheduled removal of VAT on household electricity for six months and cut business rates for pubs.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Wants care on NHS universal principles and criticised means-testing of pensions in care charges.

notes:
Positions shift over time: voted for the Iraq war but later said he would not do so again; earlier supported trans people using facilities matching their gender but backed single-sex rules in 2026; favoured a graduate tax and later tuition-fee abolition. Where a 2026 position as Prime Minister differs from earlier ones, the most recent is used. Many statements are null because no direct evidence was found.

Merged with an independent claude-sonnet-5-5 audit: 30 answers taken from it, 29 agreed, 0 conflicts settled by the integrator.

claude-sonnet-5-5 notes: Positions shifted over time: voted for Iraq war (2003), later regretted; moved from New Labour continuity (2010) to a more public-ownership stance (2015, 2026); on the EU, said he wanted to rejoin in his lifetime but promised not to re-run Brexit during the by-election, then as PM said Brexit did more harm than good and sought closer integration. Immigration answers rest partly on allies' reports and are low. Transcript sources use only Burnham's own lines.
